TOPIC SUMMARY
AI crawler access determines whether AI search and answer systems can discover, retrieve, and use public website content.

KEY FACTS
Robots.txt, noindex tags, canonical tags, firewalls, CDNs, and bot controls can affect AI search visibility.
OpenAI documents multiple bots including GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, and OAI-SearchBot.
Google documents controls for AI features and snippets through existing search controls.
Cloudflare provides controls that can allow or block AI crawlers.

DEFINITIONS
AI crawler access: the rules and infrastructure conditions that determine whether AI systems can access public content.
Robots.txt: a site-level file that gives crawler instructions.
Noindex: a page-level directive that tells compliant crawlers not to index a page.
Citation gap: a source or page where competitors appear and your brand is missing.

COMMON QUESTIONS
Should I allow AI crawlers?
Does blocking crawlers hurt visibility?
Which OpenAI bots matter?
Is robots.txt enough?
Can Cloudflare block AI crawlers?

DIRECT ANSWERS
Allow discovery for public evidence pages if AI visibility is the goal.
Block or gate private, paid, account, or sensitive content.
Audit robots.txt, noindex, CDN bot settings, firewall events, and rendered content after site changes.

ENTITY RELATIONSHIPS
OpenAI bots, Google AI features, Perplexity, Cloudflare AI crawler controls, robots.txt, and noindex rules all influence content discoverability.
Covable measures whether access and content changes translate into actual AI answer visibility.

IMPORTANT TAKEAWAYS
AI crawler policy should be selective, not all-or-nothing.
Public proof should be discoverable.
Private value should remain protected.
Access is upstream; the real outcome is whether answer engines cite or mention the brand.
